Additionally, the Reserve Bank of India's increased dollar forward position suggests a possible dollar-buying approach. Overall, market sentiment reflects caution as global factors continue to influence local currency trends.

stories.headline: Hypertension or diabetes before pregnancy linked to higher risk of fetal heart defects
stories.what_happened: Women with chronic hypertension (high blood pressure before pregnancy or diagnosed before 20 weeks of pregnancy) had a 30% higher risk of having a baby with critical congenital heart disease, the most severe form of heart defects, when compared to women with normal blood pressure before and during pregnancy, according to new independent, preliminary research presented at the American Heart Association's Scientific Sessions 2026, held Nov. 6–9 in Chicago.

stories.headline: Cardiac arrest ICU admissions rose with outdoor heat, especially in women, older adults
stories.what_happened: As daily temperatures climbed above 90 degrees Fahrenheit (F) (32 degrees Celsius) across the U.S., so did the rate of out-of-hospital (OHCA) cardiac arrest admissions to hospitals' intensive care units (ICUs). However, the heat didn't appear to affect the overall outcomes of people admitted for cardiac arrest during heat waves compared with other times, according to new, independent, preliminary research to be presented at the American Heart Association's Resuscitation Science Symposium 2026.

stories.headline: Wearable devices + AI analysis may predict high blood pressure crisis up to 3 days early

stories.headline: Survey finds gaps in use of cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome tools
stories.what_happened: In a survey of health clinics participating in a new initiative to improve care for cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome, most sites reported conducting basic screening for heart, kidney and metabolic risks. However, far fewer are using newer guideline-recommended tools such as the CKM syndrome staging framework and the American Heart Association's PREVENT (Predicting Risk of cardiovascular EVENT) equations, according to new, preliminary research presented at the American Heart Association's Scientific Sessions 2026, held Nov. 6–9 in Chicago.
